One roof, three rooms

Walk it with us.

A grocery run, a butcher counter and a hot lunch — all at the same address.

The aisles

Piñatas overhead, groceries underneath.

Mexican candies and dried chiles, a wall of hot sauces, drinks and dairy, and whole Chula piñas stacked in the crate they arrived in. The kind of shelf you can’t find anywhere else on the Plateau.

“Very friendly. Prices are good! Clean store! Definitely shop here as much as possible!”Shelby R. · Yelp

The butcher’s case

Cut and seasoned in-house.

Carne asada and chorizo out of the case, not off a shrink-wrapped shelf — and the same counter that stocks the taquería with cabeza, barbacoa, lengua and tripa.

“Their tacos asada are to die for! This is also a traditional Mexican market much like you see in Mexico.”David L. · Yelp

The kitchen in the back

Order at the counter, take a red vinyl seat.

Street tacos on checkered paper, platters big enough for the table, and horchata de coco made fresh every day. Eat in at the little dining corner or carry it home with the groceries.

“This market has a taqueria inside which served up a delicious veggie burrito that was served quickly and was reasonably priced.”Michael Jensen · Google

A house tradition

Taco Tuesday

Every Tuesday the taquería runs its specials — the one thing they post about all week.

Tres reinas — three queens

Three crowns over the door.

The name means Three Queens, and the three gold crowns ride everything the family puts its name on — the sign band over Cole Street, the carnicería poster on the back wall, the mugs behind the register.

It’s the only market of its kind on the Plateau: a full grocery run, a butcher counter and a hot kitchen at one address, run by one family who kept it a real mercado instead of a corner store.
